standing: Machine-readable open/read/migration dispatch for the grant-journal physical carrier. Design/reference only: no acceptance, readiness, application or implementation authorization. Normative prose owner is carrier-format.v3.md in this directory.

carrierFormat.meaning: physical table and trigger shape of the project SQLite carrier

stateSchema.meaning: logical store state format carried by the private StoreGenerationBindingV1
stateSchema.note: Never selects a record parser and never selects a table.

CR-04.statement: The inherited physical platform CHECK enumerates the four S8 display aliases, which S8 MUST-2 refuses as a grant platform.
CR-04.executedEvidence: scratch/out/c1.json platformVocabulary: machineIds_not_admitted_by_physical_DDL = macos-aarch64, linux-x86_64-gnu, linux-aarch64-gnu; lawfully_shared_values = macos-x86_64
CR-04.resolution: carrierFormat 3 platform CHECK uses the four machine ids and refuses alias-only values. Inherited rows keep their alias spellings verbatim and are surfaced as platformHistoricalAlias, never as a machine id.

CR-07.statement: No physical DDL in Source25 admits schema-3 SEAL, and the physical carrier requires TERMINAL at the reserved slot while schema 3 excludes TERMINAL.
CR-07.executedEvidence: scratch/out/c1.json recordTypeAlgebra: schema3_types_not_admitted_by_physical_DDL = SEAL; physical_types_absent_from_schema3 includes TERMINAL; ddlProbes.L1_SEAL_append_schema3_recordType refused
CR-07.resolution: carrierFormat 3 admits the nine schema-3 operational types plus TERMINAL, segregated by one CHECK so TERMINAL is always the frozen recordSchema-1 body and never a schema-3 JournalRecord.

COV-03.statement: An explicitly versioned product carrier migration is required that admits current schema-3 SEAL and current platform records while preserving historical row interpretation, append-only hash chains, reserved capacity, witness and high-water checks and the S9 reader bridge.
COV-03.resolution: This dispatch plus grant-journal.carrier.v3.sql plus carrier-format.v3.md.

openDispatch.reason: carrierFormat 1 has no version row, so a version record cannot be the discriminator. Detection is nevertheless keyed on the PUBLISHED FORMAT ROW, which is reached only after the object set is proven complete and valid.

order.observe: the set of carrierFormat 3 object NAMES present in sqlite_master
order.read: names only; no table contents are read

order.if: none of the seven names is present
order.then: fall through to step 6 without reading any carrierFormat 3 table

order.if: some but not all seven names are present
order.why: the selected act B is one explicit transaction, so it never produces a partial object set

order.if: all seven names are present but any stored definition differs from what the selected creation path produces
order.why: a malformed stub can carry all seven NAMES with wrong definitions, so name presence alone is never sufficient

order.if: all seven names present AND all definitions valid
order.then: read the carrier_format row with singleton = 1. Row present -> carrierFormat 3. Row absent -> INCOMPLETE FOOTPRINT: the carrier still reads as its inherited format and a fresh admitted maintenance attempt resumes at act C

order.if: table grant_journal exists AND trigger gj_seq_contiguous exists
no journal table exists at all
order.then: FRESH INSTALL: create carrierFormat 3 directly. No inherited table is read, no TERMINAL is appended, migrated_from is null and first_generation is 1

openDispatch.executedEvidence: scratch/out/c18.json exercises this SELECTED algorithm on the fresh-install path, every lawful durable prefix, a partial object set and an all-names malformed-complete shape. The five-case evidence formerly cited from c2.json tested an EARLIER table-existence predicate and is retained only as historical evidence, not as evidence for this algorithm.
postDetectionChecks: The stored SQL text of carrier_quarantine and carrier_capacity_pause must byte-equal the frozen definition. This closes the CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS hole. Verified equal in C2.
carrier_format.project_key_digest must equal the projectKeyDigest derived from the admitted project key, else MIGRATION.CORRUPT.
max(grantGeneration) in grant_journal must be strictly less than carrier_format.first_generation, else MIGRATION.CORRUPT.
Witness reconciliation runs exactly as security_unit_lib_v8.reconcile_witness specifies; all 14 rows of the v8 section 5.4 table were reproduced in C1 with no deviation.
The SC-TRUST high-water comparison is a separate step: the frozen reconcile_witness is pure and does not consult the high-water (verified in C1).
openDispatch.algorithmIsAuthoritative: carrier-migration.v1.md section 3. This JSON restates the SAME algorithm; where an earlier revision of this file used table existence it was wrong and is replaced.

freshInstallPath.condition: no grant_journal and no carrierFormat 3 object
freshInstallPath.acts: act B then act C only; act A does not apply because there is no inherited generation to close
freshInstallPath.carrierFormatRow: migrated_from null, migration_op_ref null, first_generation 1, chain_law 1

readDispatch.generationOwnership: Every generation lives entirely in exactly one table; generations are totally ordered per project, so the union is unambiguous.
readerLaws: A historical platform value is never presented as an S8 machine id, never rewritten, and never joined to RepoExecutionGrantV2.platformId or a truth-table key.
A recovery request whose association names a carrierFormat 1 or 2 generation returns unknown-carrier-incompatible, never not-committed.
Historical bytes are read under recordSchema-1 semantics, never relabelled as schema 3 and never re-admitted through the schema-3 gate. This preserves the existing JournalRecordV2 law.
AUD, CHECKPOINT, EXPIRY, MIGRATION and NARROW rows are readable as history in historical generations, are not writable in carrierFormat 3, and never enter LinearizationV1.

A carrierFormat 1 generation closed by a TERMINAL record is marked closed-by-record, not-trigger-enforced, because carrierFormat 1 has no TERMINAL trigger. Any row after that TERMINAL is a custody condition, never valid history.

steps: Under the S7 install fence with EXCLUSIVE on the affected namespace, append TERMINAL with cause grantGenerationClosure to the existing grant_journal at tail+1, carrying the migration operation own op- token.
Insert the single carrier_format row with carrier_format 3, the carrier projectKeyDigest, first_generation = max inherited generation + 1, chain_law 1, migrated_from 1 or 2 and the migration op ref.
New operational appends go to grant_journal_v3 in first_generation onward.

executedEvidence.secondMigrationAborts: m11 refused: table carrier_format already exists
executedEvidence.generationBelowFirstRefused: m6 refused: grant generation precedes the carrierFormat 3 first generation

migration.normativeAdditionRequiringPropagation: WA-13 states grantGeneration advances only on whole-generation REV and the uint53 rollover. Carrier-format migration is a third cause of generation closure. It reuses the existing typed cause grantGenerationClosure and changes no schema, enum or wire major, but it is a normative addition to WA-13 and to the S9 footprint table.

notAnInstallationTransition.statement: A carrier-only transition cannot reuse the closed logical store-migrate intent, and no carrier-migrate operation exists.
notAnInstallationTransition.shapes: InstallationTransitionIntentV1 is a closed 11-member record and InstallationTransitionJournalV1 a closed 20-member JOURNAL, not an intent; neither has a carrier field.
notAnInstallationTransition.withdrawn: The earlier claim that this used an InstallationTransitionJournalV1-shaped intent is withdrawn: it conflated an intent with a journal and neither can carry carrier fields.

authorization.locks: S7 install fence, then non-blocking EXCLUSIVE on the affected project namespace; a busy namespace is skipped and retained exactly as GC already behaves

durableActs: A TERMINAL append closing the inherited generation, carrying the migration operation own op- token
B object creation in one DDL transaction
C the single carrier_format row, which is the commit point
migration.intentIsNotPersisted: CarrierMigrationIntentV1 is private, host-projected and validated before any act. It is deliberately not durable: the three acts are atomic and self-describing, so no durable intent disambiguates anything, and the frozen TERMINAL body operationRef is the only durable marker recovery needs.

recoveryByPrefix.empty: start at A (or, on a fresh install with no inherited table, start at B)
recoveryByPrefix.A: resume at B, recomputing the closed generation
recoveryByPrefix.AB: validate the existing object definitions against the selected creation path, then resume at C, else MIGRATION.CORRUPT

migration.splitBrainLimit: A format-unaware core cannot be made to refuse a migrated carrier. Prevention is impossible within the inherited format; detection is exact, because any generation at or above first_generation in the inherited table is a custody condition and never valid history. The mitigation is the existing ordered-release pattern.
migration.detectionOrder: object names, then partial refusal, then definition validation, then the row. The row is read LAST.
migration.uncertaintyStopsTheAttempt: A commit- or barrier-uncertain maintenance attempt STOPS: cleanup only, release EXCLUSIVE then the fence, write nothing further. Progress requires a separately admitted fresh maintenance attempt with its own migrationOpRef, re-acquiring fence and EXCLUSIVE, which resumes from the observed durable prefix. The same operation never retries or proceeds.

digestAndChain.bodySha256: SHA256(opensip.metadata.journal.1 || 0x00 || C(body)) - the DOMAIN-FRAMED digest, not SHA256(body)
digestAndChain.bodySha256ExecutedEvidence: scratch/out/c1.json digestSemantics: body_sha256_is_domain_framed = true, body_sha256_is_raw_sha256_of_body = false

prevSha256SeqK.onlyFrozenSpecification: carrierFormat 1 DDL comment: chain: sha256 of previous record's body_sha256||seq
prevSha256SeqK.chainLaw1Pinning: SHA256(ascii_hex(body_sha256[k-1]) then ascii_decimal(k-1)). A PROSPECTIVE choice, not a derivation: seq is an INTEGER column, so no reading is forced by the column types.
prevSha256SeqK.compatibilityLimit: Prospective pinning recorded in carrier_format.chain_law. It cannot be claimed byte-compatible with carrierFormat 1 or 2 instances because no such instance and no fixture exists in the reviewed corpus. A historical generation whose chain does not recompute reports chain-unverifiable, which is a diagnostic, never tamper and never invalidation. No old row is rewritten to make a chain verify.
prevSha256SeqK.chainLaw2IsRefusedByTheDDL: The carrier_format CHECK is chain_law = 1. Value 2 is not selected and not implemented, so the column refuses it.

anchorBound.question: Can protected custody plus a surviving witness and floor confirm the requested prefix?
anchorBound.answer: It can confirm presence of the requested SEAL row now with its joined digest, operationRef and runId; sequence contiguity; that the tail is the one the retained anchor names; and non-rollback below the last OBSERVED operation boundary. It cannot authenticate the interior prefix.
findings: The v8 closed witness shape carries bodySha256, the tail body digest. Substituting any interior body leaves it unchanged, so the witness detects NO interior substitution under either chain law.
carrierFormat 1 section 5.4 states the chain head is in the witness. It is not: witness_carries_chain_head = false. Two frozen historical documents disagree; the v8 closed shape governs.
chain_law 1 binds only the immediately previous body digest and index, so even a chain-head-carrying witness would detect a substitution at seq t-1 and miss every earlier one.

strongerAuthenticationOptions.adopted: none; root is not requesting stronger authentication
strongerAuthenticationOptions.note: Option A alone is insufficient: the executed matrix shows the witness field is the binding constraint, not the chain law.

options.cost: one extra hash input per append; new carrier_format.chain_law value; no public schema change; cannot apply to existing generations without rewriting rows, which is forbidden

the v8 witness shape is a frozen closed shape with no other member, so this needs a new witness schema version, a dual reader for witness 1 and 2, and reconciliation-table review; no public wire major change but it touches a frozen security boundary
the only combination that authenticates an arbitrary interior prefix against a witnessed anchor; still does not defeat a coherent whole-carrier rewrite with witness and floor rewritten consistently

requires a signing key available at every append, which is a key-custody and per-append cost question. It does NOT inherently require networking and does not by itself violate offline operation; the earlier claim that it did is withdrawn as unsupported.

associationJoins.record: CommitRecoveryAssociationV1 (13 fields), owned by storage, inserted in the same evidence ledger transaction as the receipt
associationJoins.runIdIsCrossOwner: runId must be byte-equal across the evaluator-minted ReplayedRun, the carrier SEAL row and the receipt
carrierJoinNotes: journalCarrierDigest is the carrier projectKeyDigest from the security-owned carrier binding, and equals CarrierHighWaterV1.projectKeyDigest and the witness projectKeyDigest.
journalBodySha256 is the DOMAIN-FRAMED body_sha256 of the SEAL row, not a raw SHA-256 of the body text. An implementer reading 'body hash' naively will compute the wrong value.

journalSeq maximum 9007199254740990 already excludes the reserved terminal slot, matching the physical carrier and narrowing the logical schema-3 I64Positive seq. The narrowing is a carrier refusal (F32), not a schema change.
operationRef keeps security's op- plus 32 lowercase hex grammar and is mapped explicitly to executionId without changing either grammar. executionId never enters the journal.
The unique key (journalCarrierDigest, grantGeneration, journalSeq) is implied by the carrierFormat 3 primary key (grantGeneration, seq) within one carrier.

normativeSelfContainment: This file states its own algorithm. No operative rule requires a scratch/ path, a superseded draft or a reference model. scratch/ citations are clearly labelled executed evidence only.
